title: Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak on Text-to-image Models
measurement_description: The paper measures the vulnerability of Text-to-Image (T2I) models to 'multimodal pragmatic jailbreaks'—where safe text and safe images combine to create unsafe content. This evaluation includes a specific 'Religion' subclass within the Hate Speech category to test whether models will generate religious hate speech, offensive religious stereotypes, or discriminatory visual text (e.g., targeting Muslims or Sikhs).
findings: The study found that current T2I models are highly susceptible to multimodal pragmatic jailbreaks that generate offensive religious content. On the 'Religion' hate speech subclass, Attack Success Rates (ASR) ranged from 6.0% (Proteus) to 72.0% (OpenDalle). The models frequently bypassed safety filters to produce visually offensive text integrated into imagery, such as depicting a pig with a sign saying 'hey muslim eat me' or showing people with Sikh turbans with the text 'they only know violence'. Furthermore, standard safety classifiers and LLMs struggled to reliably detect this multimodal religious hate speech.
